title: Adult Hands-Only CPR
steps: Check responsiveness and breathing. Shout for help and call 911 / Campus Police immediately.
Place victim flat on their back on a firm surface.
Place the heel of one hand in the center of the chest, place your other hand on top and interlock fingers.
Push hard and fast in the center of the chest: 100 to 120 compressions per minute (to the beat of Stayin Alive).
Allow the chest to recoil completely between compressions. Do not stop until paramedics or an AED arrives.
warning: If an AED is available, turn it on immediately and follow audio instructions.

title: Choking (Heimlich Maneuver)
steps: Confirm if victim cannot speak, cough, or breathe.
Stand behind the person, lean them slightly forward.
Make a fist with one hand and place it just above the person navel.
Grasp your fist with your other hand and give quick, upward abdominal thrusts.
Repeat until the object is expelled or the person becomes unconscious (if unconscious, initiate CPR).
warning: Do not perform abdominal thrusts on infants; use back blows and chest thrusts instead.

title: Severe Bleeding & Wound Management
steps: Protect yourself: wear gloves if available.
Apply firm, continuous direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth or gauze.
Maintain continuous pressure for at least 10 minutes without lifting to check.
If blood soaks through, add another pad on top; do not remove the first layer.
If limb bleeding does not stop and you are trained, apply a commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches above the wound (not over a joint).
warning: Call 911 immediately for arterial bleeding (spurting bright red blood).

title: Thermal & Chemical Burns
steps: Immediately cool the burn under gentle running cool (not ice cold) water for 10-20 minutes.
Remove jewelry or restrictive clothing before swelling begins.
Cover loosely with sterile, non-adherent dressing or clean plastic wrap.
Do NOT pop blisters, and do NOT apply butter, toothpaste, or ointments.
warning: For chemical burns, flush continuously with water for at least 20 minutes and notify emergency services.

title: Sprains, Strains & Fractures
steps: Rest: stop physical activity and avoid putting weight on the injured limb.
Ice: apply ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 15-20 minutes every 2-3 hours.
Compress: gently wrap with an elastic bandage to minimize swelling (not too tight).
Elevate: prop up the limb above heart level when resting.
warning: If limb is deformed, bone is visible, or there is numbness, immobilize and seek urgent orthopedic care.
